chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I asked my brother Musa (peace be upon him) about a man who broke a pigeon's egg and in the egg were chicks that had moved. He said: 'He must give charity for every chick that had moved with a sheep, and give charity with its meat if he is in ihsar (state of pilgrimage ritual constraint). And if the chick had not moved, he must give charity with its value, four dirhams, which he uses to buy fodder and scatter for the pigeons of the Haram.'

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And whoever throws something of the game and wounds it, then proceeds on his way, and does not know whether it is alive or dead, then upon him is its ransom.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for breaking a pigeon egg containing a moving chick while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific fidya (compensation) for accidentally killing game while in ihram, distinguishing between a chick that has moved (requiring the sacrifice of a sheep) and one that has not (requiring the value of fodder). The Sheikh’s addition addresses the legal principle of uncertainty (istishab) when a wounded animal is left behind, ensuring the pilgrim fulfills their obligation even if the animal's status is unknown. This ruling highlights the precision of Shia jurisprudence in balancing ritual purity with practical economic compensation.
